llm.reply:
KRAS encodes a small GTPase, a member of the mammalian ras gene family [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. A single amino acid change can make it constitutively activating [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"]. None of the findings name a specific Gene Ontology molecular activity term, so the GTPase assignment rests on the RefSeq gene summary.

## GTPase Function

The OMIM record names the gene as a protooncogene GTPase [4]. Its product switches between an active GTP-bound state and an inactive GDP-bound state [30: "binding both the active (GTP-bound) and inactive (GDP-bound) forms of KRAS"]. Activity is driven by a guanosine exchange factor [28: "the cognate guanosine exchange factor (GEF) Son of Sevenless 1 that drives KRAS"].

## Oncogenic Signaling Consequences

The mutant, transforming protein is linked to several cancers [11: "implicated in various malignancies, including lung adenocarcinoma, mucinous adenoma, ductal carcinoma of the pancreas and colorectal carcinoma"]. In colorectal cancer, oncogenic KRAS switches on a transcription factor that pushes fibroblast remodeling [27: "KRAS* activates the transcription factor CP2 (TFCP2) that upregulates the expression of the proadipogenic factors BMP4 and WNT5B"].

## Isoforms

Alternative splicing gives two protein forms [11: "variants encoding two isoforms that differ in the C-terminal region"].

The KRAS gene product is a small GTPase [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. Its OMIM entry is titled KRAS PROTOONCOGENE, GTPase; KRAS [4]. It cycles between an active GTP-bound state and an inactive GDP-bound state [30: "both the active (GTP-bound) and inactive (GDP-bound) forms of KRAS"].

## Gene identity

The gene symbol is KRAS [1]. The gene name is KRAS [5]. The literature entity name is Kras [6]. A single amino acid change can activate the protein, and the resulting transforming protein is linked to lung, pancreatic and colorectal cancers [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"][11: "including lung adenocarcinoma, mucinous adenoma, ductal carcinoma of the pancreas and colorectal carcinoma"].

## Regulation and signaling

KRAS is driven by the guanine nucleotide exchange factor Son of Sevenless 1 [28: "the cognate guanosine exchange factor (GEF) Son of Sevenless 1 that drives KRAS"]. In colorectal cancer, oncogenic KRAS activates TFCP2, which reprograms fibroblasts to support angiogenesis [27: "KRAS* activates the transcription factor CP2 (TFCP2)"]. The related paper is Oncogenic KRAS Drives Lipofibrogenesis to Promote Angiogenesis and Colon Cancer Progression. [9].

## Variants

One ClinVar record is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.458ATG[1] (p.Asp154del) [3]. Another is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.36T>C (p.Gly12=) [10]. Another is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.337C>T (p.Leu113=) [15]. Another is NM_033360.4(KRAS):c.524A>G (p.Glu175Gly) [19]. Another is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.417T>A (p.Ile139=) [23].

## Therapeutic targeting

KRAS was long regarded as undruggable, but G12C inhibitors such as sotorasib have now been approved [26: "AMG510 was the first drug-targeting KRAS (G12C) to be approved for clinical use"]. That review is titled KRAS mutation: from undruggable to druggable in cancer. [2]. Most pancreatic KRAS mutations are not G12C, so G12C inhibitors do not apply to them [28: "G12D (44%), G12V (34%) and G12R (20%) that are not amenable to treatment"]. That paper is titled Targeting KRAS in pancreatic cancer. [14]. A degrader molecule breaks down most common oncogenic KRAS variants [29: "degrades 13 out of 17 of the most prevalent oncogenic KRAS alleles"]. That paper is titled Targeting cancer with small-molecule pan-KRAS degraders. [18]. A pan-KRAS inhibitor binds within the switch-II pocket [30: "engages the switch-II pocket through a water-mediated hydrogen-bond network"]. That paper is titled A pan-KRAS inhibitor and its derived degrader elicit multifaceted anti-tumor efficacy in KRAS-driven cancers. [22]. Related publications include PMID 34776511 [8]. Another is PMID 37768068 [13]. Another is PMID 38686056 [17]. Another is PMID 39298590 [21]. Another is PMID 40780213 [25]. One trial is Sorafenib in Combination With Irinotecan in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patients With KRAS Mutated Tumors [7]. Another is PREMIUM, Observational Study [12]. Another is A Trial of mFOLFIRI With MEK162 in Patients With Advanced RAS (HRAS, NRAS, or KRAS) Positive Metastatic Colorectal Cancers [16]. Another is Frequency of EGFR and KRAS Mutations and Clinical-prognostic Correlation in Brazilian Lung Cancer Patients [20]. Another is A Phase 1/2, Study Evaluating the Safety, Tolerability, PK, and Efficacy of Sotorasib (AMG 510) in Subjects With Solid Tumors With a Specific KRAS Mutation (CodeBreaK 100) [24].
